title: New Course, Same Old Chaos
title_candidates: Williams Sets The Pace In Portugal
theme: TEG's first visit to Quinta da Marinha proves the venue may be new but the script is reassuringly familiar.
tone: Wry restraint throughout, treating a bogey at the ocean-view 3rd with the gravity of a diplomatic incident.
opening_hook: TEG made its first landfall at Quinta da Marinha on Wednesday, and inside three holes the new course had already claimed a scalp: Henry Meller's quintuple-bogey ten leaving him rooted to the bottom of the Wooden Spoon table before most of the field had reached the turn.

round_story.subject: Gregg Williams's stableford surge to 38 points, the best round of the opening day at Quinta da Marinha
round_story.why_it_matters: It's the platform from which Williams grabs an immediate share of the TEG 8 Trophy lead, though a rough closing stretch shows the round wasn't without its wobbles.
round_story.shape: Williams sits quietly in touch through the front nine before catching fire from the 8th, reeling off 14 stableford points in a four-hole burst that includes a birdie at the 10th to snatch the outright Trophy lead; the back nine then turns scratchy, with a run of holes between the 12th and 15th yielding almost nothing including a quadruple bogey at the 15th, but the cushion built earlier proves enough to see him home in front.
headline_candidates: Williams Surges Clear At The Turn
Early Charge Puts Williams In Front
Williams Sets The Pace In Portugal
round_story.chosen_headline: Williams Surges Clear At The Turn
round_story.standfirst: A four-hole blitz from the 8th hands Gregg Williams the outright TEG 8 Trophy lead despite a shaky finish.

race_story.subject: The opening skirmish for the TEG 8 Green Jacket, with David Mullin edging ahead of Jon Baker by a single shot
race_story.why_it_matters: With four rounds still to play the gap is paper-thin, and Jon Baker's own round shows exactly how quickly it could have gone the other way.
race_story.shape: The Green Jacket lead changes hands repeatedly through the outward half, level at the 6th and again at the 10th and 11th, before David Mullin edges clear with a par at the 13th; Jon Baker, meanwhile, survives a quintuple bogey at that same hole to stay within touch, a birdie at the 17th arresting the damage just in time.
headline_candidates: Mullin Edges Ahead By A Single Shot
Mullin Takes Early Green Jacket Lead
Baker Survives A Nine To Stay Close
race_story.chosen_headline: Mullin Takes Early Green Jacket Lead
race_story.standfirst: David Mullin's par at the 13th settles a Green Jacket lead that changed hands three times inside the first round.

discovered_storylines.subject: Stuart Neumann's opening-round collapse, the worst Trophy round recorded in TEG history to date, which settles him at the foot of the TEG 8 Wooden Spoon table by a distance
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: It's only round one, but a 12-point cushion at the bottom already looks like a headache for the rest of the week, and it briefly cost Henry Meller his own unwanted tenancy of last place.
discovered_storylines.shape: Henry Meller's quintuple-bogey 10 at the 3rd first drops him to the bottom of the Wooden Spoon race; Stuart Neumann then goes one nine-hole stretch worse, bleeding 29 shots between the 7th and 15th with quintuple bogeys at both the 12th and the 14th; by the close Neumann's 17 points is the worst Trophy round logged in the competition's history, and he inherits last place with room to spare.
discovered_storylines.standfirst: A calamitous run from the 7th to the 15th leaves Stuart Neumann with the worst round in TEG history and an early lock on the Wooden Spoon.

race_state_note: This is the opening round of TEG 8, so all standings reflect the first measurements of the tournament; there is no prior state to compare against.
